messages:
rachel: Quick hit: ran a compact bring-up for atlas-9b (int8 baseline, int6, int4-slim) against a mixed GTN slice set. posting compact findings + a suggested routing/playbook for product/GTN. TL;DR: int6 looks like the best tradeoff for most short-form workloads; int4-slim is very cheap but has heavier regression on longform.

dan: numbers please. product wants a simple paragraph to share.

rachel: core numbers (median prompt ~50 tok, mixed seqs):
- int8 baseline: p50 85ms, p95 230ms, throughput 240 tok/s, unit cost $0.0105/token-eq
- int6: p50 98ms, p95 270ms, throughput 290 tok/s, unit cost $0.0067/token-eq (~36% cheaper)
- int4-slim: p50 110ms, p95 360ms, throughput 330 tok/s, unit cost $0.0052/token-eq (~50% cheaper)
quality quick checks (aggregated GTN slices, n~7.2k):
- short QA EM: int8 81.2%, int6 80.1% (-1.1 pts), int4-slim 78.0% (-3.2 pts)
- rerank proxy NDCG: int8 0.735, int6 0.730 (-0.7%), int4-slim 0.716 (-2.6%)
- longform summarization ROUGE-proxy: int8 0.66, int6 0.62 (-6.1%), int4-slim 0.54 (-18.2%)
- hallucination proxy: int8 3.2%, int6 3.9%, int4-slim 6.1%
notes: longform slice small (~900) -> high variance. short-form slices large and stable.

kevin: p95 for int4-slim is high. any runtime explanation?

rachel: int4-slim uses an experimental GEMM pack; a subset of long sequences triggers a fallback path that increases tail. infra tuning (batch shape, enable fused-attn) reduces p95 substantially. we'll open a kernel ticket.

infra-bot: ticket created #KERNEL-7901 to investigate int4-slim fallback and batch tuning (owner: @kevin). ETA 72h.

priya: product context : most GTN traffic is rerank/snippet; longform is critical for top enterprise customers. we need routing by intent and per-customer opt-outs.

dan: propose routing + rollback plan? keep it conservative.

rachel: suggested routing/playbook (compact):
```
routes:
  - name: high-volume-short
    match: intent in ["search_snippet","rerank","qa_short"]
    traffic: { int6: 0.75, int4-slim: 0.15, int8: 0.10 }
  - name: conversation-and-assistant
    match: intent in ["assistant_chat","user_session"]
    traffic: { int6: 0.6, int8: 0.4 }
  - name: longform-sensitive
    match: intent in ["summarize_long","document_analysis"]
    traffic: { int8: 1.0 }
monitored_metrics: ["QA_EM","NDCG_proxy","ROUGE_proxy","hallucination_rate","latency_p95","cost_per_1k_tokens"]
canary: 1% for 1h -> 5% for 4h -> 25% for 12h; require no slice QA_EM drop >1.2 pts and latency_p95 stable
rollback_rules:
  - if any slice QA_EM drops >1.5 pts absolute over 30m -> rollback that slice to int8
  - if hallucination_rate increases >1.0% abs -> pause rollout and alert
  - if cost savings < 20% for eligible traffic -> reassess rollout
```

kevin: +1. add per-customer min-sample threshold so noisy small slices don't trigger global rollback. also log token-type breakdown to validate priming/cache benefits.

priya: GTN summary bullets (single paragraph for product):
- Recommendation: adopt atlas-9b int6 as default for short-form and rerank workloads; enable int4-slim for ultra-high-volume snippet traffic where acceptable. Expect ~36% token unit cost reduction with int6 vs current int8 baseline; int4-slim offers ~50% reduction but with larger regressions on longform. Longform should remain on int8 pending kernel fixes and expanded evals. Canary and per-slice rollback required.

dan: $ example for GTN customers: give mid-market (40M tok/mo) and enterprise (150M tok/mo, 30% longform).

rachel: quick math:
- Mid-market 40M tok/mo, if 70% eligible -> 28M * (0.0105 - 0.0067) = $104.8k/mo gross; realistic eligible share 60% -> ~$90k/mo saved.
- Enterprise 150M tok/mo, 30% longform -> eligible = 105M * (0.0105 - 0.0067) = $393.6k/mo gross; realistic 60% eligible -> ~$236k/mo saved.
notes: assumes billed token-eq consistent; priming-heavy workloads change effective savings.

infra-bot: canary deployment started for route "high-volume-short" -> 1% at 1701013945 :rotating_light:

kevin: action items: 1) infra runs kernel tuning #KERNEL-7901, 2) rachel to run 2-day slice A/B focusing longform (20k samples) to tighten CI, 3) priya to draft GTN comms + opt-out flow, 4) dan to approve product one-paragraph and send to GTN.

rachel: will post GTN note & attach per-slice CSVs in 45m. thanks all :thumbsup:
